scope: Frozen real-image queue benchmark. A pass certifies this workload only. Original ANS research promotion criteria remain separate.

science.cache: immutable raw data, metadata and template only; recompute all pixel products for every live occurrence

reference: fixed4: one mosaic request at a time in admission order, up to four independent frame projections; shared secondary reference fills spare workers with the oldest ready request
current: Unmodified v5_full at 22676ec9848b4b28cb84edd73b61e5eef630bd55, legacy_instant observation clock, one honest tick per minute; 207 internal units control weighted work-conserving dispatch on four nonpreemptive CPU slots; one completed mosaic = 256 internal work units. Stage service charges use measured busy worker-seconds; stage queues use mosaic-equivalents. Policy sees only arrivals, sampled queues, known workers and delivered service.

scoring.reuse: Stable public regression benchmark; tune using development only. Shared streams and service demands across arms. No post-result threshold changes. This is not a blind external validation.

request_mix.processing: tiles of a request produced in order; frame projections may overlap, then background, then coadd. Waiting time starts at scheduled submission.

live.hardware: same four allowed logical CPUs, one process per slot, no cross-job output reuse; isolated runs on the same CPU set
live.reference_quality: Every science/area pair must match the corresponding independently run reference Montage workflow on the same canonical input tables; compare reproducible FITS images or canonical pixel payload plus WCS. Missing work invalidates the score.

aggregation: pool paired end-to-end request latencies across equal-size streams; linear empirical percentiles. Family checks separately. PASS only if all gates hold, incomplete evidence = NOT EVALUATED; a performance breach = FAIL. Gain requires both replay and live evidence. Log every official attempt.
selection: Freeze service profile, workload manifests, baseline runner and scoring before the official runs. Generate candidates using development scores only; prioritize gate violations, then normalized excess over gates, then mean latency, then ID. Future candidates use the same benchmark. No oracle service times, future admissions or fault labels in schedulers.
